The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. The Israelites said, “Tell us how this evil happened.”
The Levite, the husband of the woman who had been killed, answered them, “My concubine and I came into Gibeah of Benjamin to spend the night.
The men of Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house where I was during the night. They wanted to kill me, and they violated my concubine, and she died.
I took my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout all the lands of Israel’s inheritance, because they had committed sin and wickedness in Israel.
Look, all of you are Israelites. Give your judgment and advice about this.”
All the people rose as one and said, “None of us will go to his tent, and none of us will turn aside to his house.
Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will cast lots against it.

Let us select ten men out of every hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to obtain provisions for the people who are crossing over to go against Gibeah of Benjamin, in response to all the wickedness they have committed in Israel.”
All the men of Israel gathered against the town as one, united.
All the tribes of Israel sent men to all those of the house of Benjamin, saying, “What is this evil that has happened among you?
Now hand over the wicked men who are in Gibeah, so that we may put them to death and remove the evil from Israel.” But the Benjaminites would not listen to their fellow Israelites.
All the Benjaminites gathered from their towns at Gibeah to go out and fight against the Israelites.
On that day, the Benjaminites mustered twenty-six thousand men armed with swords from their towns, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who mustered seven hundred men.
whose right hands were disabled. Every one of them could sling a stone at a hair without missing.
The men of Israel, excluding the Benjaminites, mustered four hundred thousand men armed with swords, all of them fighting men.
They arose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God. The Israelites said, “Who should go up first for us to fight against the Benjaminites?” The LORD said, “Judah first.”
The Israelites rose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.
The Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and drew up in battle formation against Israel. On that day, when they fought against them, they struck down twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground.
The Israelites rallied again and once more drew up their battle line in the place where they had drawn it up on the first day.

The Israelites went up and wept before the Lord until evening. They inquired of the Lord, saying, “Should we again go into battle against our brothers, the Benjaminites?” The Lord said, “Go up against them.”
The Israelites fought against the Benjaminites on the next day.
On the second day the Benjaminites came out from Gibeah to meet them, and once again the Benjaminites struck down eighteen thousand Israelites to the ground, all of them armed with swords.

All the Israelites, the entire people, went up and came to Bethel. They wept and sat there before the Lord. They fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
The Israelites inquired of the Lord. The ark of the Lord was there in those days,

Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, was serving before him in those days. They asked, “Should we again go out to battle against our brothers, the Benjaminites, or should we stop?” The Lord said, “Go up, because tomorrow I will hand them over to you.”
The Israelites set an ambush against Gibeah and surrounded it.
The Israelites went up against the Benjaminites on the third day and took up their battle positions against Gibeah as before.

The Benjaminites came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began striking down some of the people along the roads, one going up to Gibeah and the other to Bethel, in the open country—about thirty men of Israel.
The Benjaminites said, “They are being defeated before us as they were at first.” But the Israelites said, “Let us flee and draw them out of the town onto the road.”
All the Israelites rose from their positions and took up their battle formation at Baal-tamar. The Israelites lying in ambush were watching from their position, from the cave at Gibeah.
Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gibeah, and the battle grew fierce. But the Benjaminites did not know that disaster had come upon them.
The Lord defeated Benjamin before Israel. That day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred Benjaminites, all of them armed with swords.
The Benjaminites saw that they had been defeated. The Israelites had given ground to the men of Benjamin because they trusted the men they had placed in ambush against Gibeah.
The men lying in ambush fell quietly upon Gibeah. They advanced and put the whole town to the sword.
The men of Israel had arranged with those lying in ambush that they should send up a rising column of smoke from the town.

The men of Israel retreated from the battle, and Benjamin began striking down Israelites, killing thirty men. They were saying, “They are certainly being defeated before us, as in the earlier battles.”
Smoke began rising from the town like a pillar. The Benjaminites looked behind them, and there was the town’s cloud of smoke rising to the sky.
The men of Israel turned against them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified because they saw that disaster was closing in on them.
They fled before the Israelites toward the wilderness road, but the battle overtook them, and those in front [?] them in the middle.
They pursued Benjamin and drove them away, destroying them with ease as far as the area opposite Gibeah on the east.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them fighting men.

They turned and fled into the wilderness toward the rock of Rimmon. Five thousand men armed with swords fell along the road. The Israelites pursued them as far as Gibeon and killed two thousand more of them.
In all, twenty-five thousand Benjaminites armed with swords fell that day, all of them mighty warriors.
Six hundred men turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon for four months.

The Israelites turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them down with the sword. They wiped them out in the towns, from people to livestock and everything they found. They also burned every town they found.
The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to a Benjaminite in marriage.”
They came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening. They raised their voices and wept bitterly.
They said, “Why, Lord, God of Israel, has this happened among Israel, that today one tribe should be lost from Israel?”
The next day the people rose early, built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

The Israelites said, “Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come up to the assembly before the Lord?” For a solemn oath had been sworn that anyone who did not come up before the Lord at Mizpah must surely be put to death.
The Israelites felt regret for their brothers, the Benjaminites, and said, “Today one tribe has disappeared from Israel.”
They said, “What shall we do for those who remain without wives, since we have sworn by the Lord not to give them wives?”
They asked, “Which one of the tribes of Israel did not go up before the Lord at Mizpah?” No men from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp.
The people were counted there, and no one from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was found there.
The people sent twelve thousand valiant men there and commanded them, “Go and strike down the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the sword, including the women and children.”
This is what you must do: destroy every man and every woman who has had sexual relations with a man.
Among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had not had sexual relations with men, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
The whole assembly sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.
Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women they had kept alive from among the women of Jabesh-gilead, but there were not enough for them.
And the people grieved for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a gap among the tribes of Israel.
The elders of the people said, “What shall we do for those who are left without wives, these remaining men, since the women of Benjamin have perished?
They said, “A remnant of Benjamin must be preserved, so that a tribe is not lost from Israel.
For we cannot give them wives from our daughters, because the Israelites swore, saying, ‘Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.’”
They said, “Look, a festival of the Lord takes place from time to time at Shiloh, north of Bethel, east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.
They instructed the Benjaminites, saying to them, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.

When you see the daughters of Shiloh coming out to play tambourines, come out of the vineyards and seize a wife for yourselves, each man from among the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

If their fathers or brothers come to plead their case before us, we will say to them, ‘Have compassion on them, because they did not each capture a wife in battle. You did not give the women to them, so you have not sinned.’”
The Benjaminites did so and took wives for all of themselves from among the women playing tambourines whom they seized. They returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them.
At that time the Israelites left there, each for his tribe and his clan. They departed from there, each for his own inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel, and everyone did what seemed right in his own eyes.
